comment: How each compiler driver SPELLS its options, as DATA rather than as an if-chain. The set is enumerable: a driver's option grammar is a fixed, documented thing, and every entry here is a fact about the DRIVER, never about a project. Consumer: src/flat_cmake.py, recovering a unit's own flags from its recorded command.
why_arity_matters: Arity is the only thing that has to be right. A flag that takes an operand but is counted as taking none leaves the operand behind as a bare token, and the compiler reads it as another input file. A flag with NO operand counted as taking one swallows whatever follows it. Both are silent: the build either fails far away or quietly compiles something else.

structural_pair.comment: The operand names an OUTPUT, a dependency file or a target, so it goes with the flag when the flag is dropped. Kept, `-o <path>` reaches the compiler among its options and it answers 'output filename specified twice'.

semantic_pair.comment: The operand is part of what the flag MEANS, so both travel into the unit's options.

path_pair.comment: The operand is a SEARCH PATH. -I is universal; a module directory is spelled -J by gfortran and -module by ifort/ifx, and getting that wrong is what breaks every `use` in a replay rather than anything visible at the flag itself.

link_only.comment: Belongs to a LINK, never to a compile of one source. A link line that compiles a source inside it carries these because it is also the link; leaving them in that source's compile options makes the compiler report 'linker input file unused because linking not done'.

module_dir.comment: Flags naming where MODULE files go. Removed from a unit's options: a module directory is not a per-unit fact -- it is where a whole build's modules go, and the build system needs it to work out WHICH UNIT MUST COMPILE FIRST. A `.mod` is a compile-time dependency and nothing in a flat list of sources says so. Left in a unit's options it both scatters that knowledge and suppresses the dependency scan; measured on LAPACK, whose `la_xisnan` `use la_constants` went unordered and failed on a module file not yet written. Spellings differ per driver, which is why this is a table entry and not a literal.

drop.comment: Flags with no operand that are dropped. These describe the BUILD's own mechanics -- which intermediate it consumes, which dependency file it writes -- and none of them is a fact about the unit. `-fpreprocessed` is the example: it is true of the intermediate this build's scan step produced, and false of the source a replay compiles.

keep_single.comment: Flags with no operand that are KEPT. A flag having no operand says nothing about whether it means something -- `-fno-automatic` and `-O3` are single tokens and both decide how the unit is compiled. Measured: collapsing these into the drop set silently removed -fno-automatic, -fno-range-check, -fallow-argument-mismatch and -O3 from every MYSTRAN unit, which changes what the code does rather than how fast it runs.

drivers.comment: basename PREFIX -> family. Asked of the executable's own basename, so /usr/bin/gfortran and a variable holding mpif90 are both recognised.
